knowledge_base: LIFELINE Communities UK community financial pressure indicators

indicators.description: Average UK monthly private rent and annual change.
indicators.denominator: Private rented properties covered by the Price Index of Private Rents
indicators.methodology: ONS Price Index of Private Rents (PIPR).
limitations: The estimate is provisional.
This is an aggregate average and does not describe every renter or property.

indicators.description: Average private rent in Southwark and annual rental inflation.
indicators.methodology: ONS local housing prices and rents visualisation using official private-rent statistics.
limitations: Average rent does not capture the distribution of rents, property size or tenant circumstances.
The local figure is an aggregate estimate.

indicators.description: Average private rent in York and annual rental inflation.
indicators.methodology: ONS local housing prices and rents visualisation using official private-rent statistics.
limitations: Average rent does not capture the distribution of rents, property size or tenant circumstances.
The local figure is an aggregate estimate.

indicators.description: Share of households in fuel poverty under the Low Income Low Energy Efficiency metric.
indicators.data_type: modelled official statistic in development at sub-regional level
indicators.methodology: LILEE counts a household as fuel poor when it is in a property with FPEER band D to G and its disposable income after housing costs and required energy costs would be below the poverty line.
limitations: Sub-regional estimates are modelled and constrained to regional totals.
They should be used for general trends and identifying particularly high or low areas, not detailed trends over time.
Fuel poverty is based on required energy costs, not actual spending.
indicators.source_name: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

indicators.indicator_name: Households in fuel poverty, West Midlands
indicators.description: Regional fuel-poverty rate under the LILEE metric.
indicators.trend: highest regional rate in England in this release
indicators.methodology: LILEE metric; regional estimates are taken from national fuel-poverty statistics.
limitations: The source cautions that sub-regional estimates are for general trends and identifying high or low areas.
This is not evidence that every household in the region is fuel poor.
indicators.source_name: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

indicators.description: Households in temporary accommodation under the statutory homelessness duty.
indicators.denominator: Households in England on the statutory homelessness duty
indicators.trend: increasing 5.0% year on year; decreasing 0.4% from previous quarter
indicators.population_affected: Households in temporary accommodation, including households with children
indicators.methodology: Quarterly statutory homelessness administrative data; temporary accommodation is a stock figure measured at the end of the quarter.
limitations: Data are provisional when first published and are revised for late updates.
A stock count on the last day of the quarter is not a count of all households experiencing homelessness during the period.
indicators.source_name: Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities

indicators.description: Households in temporary accommodation per 1,000 households in London.
indicators.trend: higher than Rest of England rate of 2.8 per 1,000
limitations: The rate is area-level and does not imply uniform experience across London.
Comparisons may reflect housing markets, local authority practice and household composition as well as need.
indicators.source_name: Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities

indicators.indicator_name: Unemployment rate, UK population aged 16 and over
indicators.description: Seasonally adjusted unemployment rate among the economically active population.
indicators.unit: percent of economically active people aged 16 and over
indicators.denominator: Economically active population aged 16 and over
indicators.trend: 0.2 percentage points higher year on year; largely unchanged on latest quarter
indicators.population_affected: People aged 16 and over in the UK labour force
indicators.methodology: Labour Force Survey estimate; unemployment is the proportion of the economically active population who are unemployed.
limitations: Survey estimates are subject to sampling and non-sampling uncertainty.
Unemployment rate is not the proportion of the total population who are unemployed.

indicators.indicator_name: Pupils eligible for free school meals
indicators.description: Percentage of pupils eligible for free school meals in England.
indicators.denominator: Pupils in state-funded primary, secondary and special schools, non-maintained special schools and state-funded alternative provision schools
indicators.trend: increasing by 0.8 percentage points; over 2.2 million pupils eligible
indicators.methodology: School census and school characteristics data for the January 2026 count.
limitations: Eligibility is a proxy for household financial circumstances and is not a direct measure of household income.
Coverage and eligibility rules are specific to the school-meals measure.

indicators.indicator_name: Emergency food parcels distributed by Trussell food banks
indicators.description: Emergency food parcels distributed by food banks in the Trussell community across the UK.
indicators.unit: emergency food parcels; more than 2.6 million
indicators.denominator: Parcels recorded by Trussell community food banks
indicators.trend: decreasing 12% from 2024 but still above pre-pandemic levels
indicators.population_affected: People receiving emergency food parcels through the Trussell community
indicators.methodology: Counts parcels supplied by Trussell community food banks; headline parcel numbers measure volume rather than unique users.
limitations: Parcels are not unique people or households.
Trussell figures do not cover all independent or non-Trussell food banks and cannot fully explain food insecurity across the UK.
The numeric value is a rounded lower-bound representation of 'over 2.6 million'.

indicators.indicator_name: Emergency food parcels distributed in Scotland
indicators.description: Emergency food parcels distributed by food banks in the Trussell community in Scotland.
indicators.denominator: Parcels recorded by Trussell community food banks in Scotland
indicators.trend: no comparable previous value in the source page
indicators.population_affected: People receiving emergency food parcels through the Trussell community in Scotland
limitations: Parcels are not unique users.
Coverage is limited to the Trussell community and is not a complete measure of food insecurity.
